parsed.modern: The true nature of artisticening thus so little known, it is no wonder to find chemists differing very much as to the class of natural bodies in which it ought to be placed. Avicenna and a great number of others class it with the sulphurs; Albertus Magnus and his follower, among the salts. Becher confides it as a kind of foam, or falcigenous body. Later experiments, however, have made it evident, that white arsenic conflicts of an acid united to phlogiston; and that by diminishing the latter, the acid becomes more and more apparent; while, on the contrary, by augmenting the quantity of phlogistic matter, the arsenic assumes the metallic form. With respect to the fulphurous nature of arsenic, it appears, indeed that the regulus itself, as well as orpiment and realgar, are inflammable substances; but it is not so with white arsenic. This inflammability, therefore, which arsenic in a certain state has in common with zinc and several other metals, will not denominate it sulphureous, any more than those of other bodies which possess the common property of inflammability can be denominated sulphur.
